px.transport: QUIC preferred with authenticated TLS fallback

xray.inner_application: HTTPS TLS with verified owned CA

config_parameters.secrets: omitted; regenerate private configs with provided scripts

notes: Every protocol uses the same fixed physical link budget; PX also has an application frame pacer.
A common source-paced background follow-up is needed to isolate generic rate-limiting gains.
Warmup runs a separate application workload; reusable proxy outer sessions persist into measurement.
All operation failures/timeouts/censoring are retained; successful-only percentiles cannot be read alone.
nstat TCP retransmission deltas include all namespace TCP sockets, including loopback proxy/fixture sockets; they do not measure QUIC retransmissions.
Resource CPU is percent of one core; guest has two vCPUs; GOMAXPROCS=1 per process.
On/off uses the same sparse-copy binary. Both endpoints explicitly set sparse_redundancy to the selected mode.
Both PX modes use default Reno, window64KiB, priority=true, adaptive=false and the same8/2Mbps app pacer.
Copy datagrams may win because of scheduling or packaging; first-delivered counters do not prove loss recovery.
Successful datagram submission can precede actual transmission. Missing shutdown counters are recorded as missing, not zero activity.
Counter logs include startup/warmup; their values are not measurement-window wire-overhead accounting.

hint_provenance.prototype: sparse delayed datagram copies; same executable in both modes
hint_provenance.counter_interpretation: sent_datagrams means accepted by QUIC; first_delivered_bytes means copy delivered first; neither proves physical loss recovery
hint_provenance.counter_scope: session lifetime including warmup; use qdisc deltas for measurement-window external byte costs
